pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The missing scarf
paragraphs: The traveller spent the morning in a café and left their coat on a chair. When it was time to leave, they put the coat on in a hurry and went to the station.
On the train, they noticed that their scarf was missing. They initially thought they had lost it between the station and the train. They had not seen anyone take it.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The café’s evidence
paragraphs: Café staff found a scarf on the chair the traveller had used. A photograph taken before the traveller’s departure also shows the scarf on that chair.
The staff kept the scarf behind the counter for collection. The photograph places it in the café before the train journey, contradicting the traveller’s first explanation.

pages.title: Tell the story of the missing scarf
pages.instruction: You are the traveller. Use the café and train timeline to tell Teacher how you found your missing scarf

pages.title: Create emphasis with negative inversion
pages.instruction: Move an auxiliary before the subject after a fronted negative expression

rows.subject: Plain word order
rows.example: I didn’t know the scarf was still at the café

rows.subject: Fronted little
rows.example: Little did I know the scarf was still at the café

rows.subject: An earlier experience
rows.example: Never had I felt so relieved to find a missing scarf

pages.note: Invert the main clause, not the following reported idea. With did, use a base verb; with had, use a past participle. This creates emphasis, not a different sequence of events.

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: The photograph changes the timeline. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I found the ending of the scarf story. The café staff discovered it on the chair where the traveller had left a coat earlier. A photograph taken before departure showed the scarf there already, so it hadn’t disappeared on the train at all. The staff kept it behind the counter, and the traveller collected it later. What made the ending surprising wasn’t a dramatic theft or a stranger’s secret plan. It was the discovery that the initial timeline was wrong. Could you retell it so I first understand the worried expectation, then see why that photograph changes the explanation? You can use a simple sentence for the revelation; an inverted phrase is only useful if it gives the moment the emphasis you want

s_mission.title: The scarf’s timeline

questions.prompt: When did the traveller notice that the scarf was missing?
questions.answer: They noticed it on the train.
questions.hint: Separate the moment of discovery from the earlier café visit.

questions.prompt: Where did the traveller initially think the scarf had been lost?
questions.answer: They initially thought it had been lost between the station and the train.
questions.hint: Find the explanation introduced by “At first”.

questions.prompt: What does the photograph show, and when was it taken?
questions.answer: It shows the scarf on the café chair before the traveller’s departure.
questions.hint: Identify both the location and the photograph’s timing.

referenceParagraphs: The traveller left a coat on a café chair, put it on in a hurry and went to the station. They only noticed that their scarf was missing once they were on the train. At first, they thought it had been lost between the station and the train.
A photograph taken before their departure shows the scarf on the café chair. The traveller had not seen anyone take it.

s_reply.title: The scarf is found

questions.prompt: What does the photograph rule out about the train journey?
questions.answer: It rules out the scarf disappearing during that train journey.
questions.hint: Compare the time of the photograph with the journey.

questions.prompt: Where did the staff keep the scarf?
questions.answer: They kept it behind the counter.
questions.hint: Find the place where the staff stored it.

questions.answer: The traveller collected the scarf from the café.
questions.hint: Look for what the traveller did after the staff found it.

referenceParagraphs: The photograph shows the scarf on the café chair before the traveller left. It had therefore been left behind before the train journey, rather than disappearing during the journey.
Café staff found it and kept it behind the counter. The traveller later collected it from the café. No theft was reported or witnessed.
